rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuking question asks whether a person imagines being left neglected, without resurrection after death.
rows.anchor: أيظن الانسان أن يترك مهملا لا يعتنى به فلا يبعث بإحيائه بعد الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suda means neglected or left unattended; such abandonment would entail no obligation and no recompense.
rows.anchor: والسدى المهمل، والمعنى أيظن الانسان أن يترك مهملا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject of kāna is an implicit pronoun referring back to the human being.
rows.anchor: اسم كان ضمير راجع إلى الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imnāʾ of semen means pouring it into the womb.
rows.anchor: وإمناء المني صبه في الرحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject that becomes a clinging clot may be the human being or the semen.
rows.anchor: أي ثم كان الإنسان - أو المني - قطعة من دم منعقد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God then measured and formed it with adjustment and completion.
rows.anchor: فقدره فصوره بالتعديل والتكميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From the human being God made the two kinds, male and female.
rows.anchor: أي فجعل من الإنسان الصنفين الذكر والأنثى

words: أَلَيْسَ ذَٰلِكَ بِقَادِرٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَن يُحْيِىَ الْمَوْتَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse argues for resurrection from God's universal power and His proven ability to create initially; bringing back the dead is easier than beginning creation.
rows.anchor: احتجاج على البعث الذي ينكرونه استبعادا له بعموم القدرة وثبوتها على الخلق الابتدائي والإعادة لا تزيد على الابتداء مؤنة بل هي أهون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that revelation weighed on the Prophet, who moved his lips to memorize; God promised to gather and recite it, told him to listen, and promised its explanation; thereafter he listened to Gabriel and recited after he left.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يعالج من التنزيل شدة، وكان يحرك به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A second report says the Prophet hurried to recite each revelation to memorize it, after which this verse was revealed; he also did not know a sūra had ended until the basmala descended.
rows.anchor: وفيه أخرج ابن المنذر وابن مردويه عن ابن عباس قال كان النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī notes similar reports from Ibn Jubayr and others, but says the fit between this explanation and the verses is obscure.
rows.anchor: روى ما في معنى صدر الحديث في المجمع عن ابن جبير وفي معناه غير واحد من الروايات، وقد

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummī glosses al-ʿājilah as the present world.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى { كلا بل تحبون العاجلة } قال الدنيا الحاضرة

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummī explains tadharūna al-ākhirah as abandoning the hereafter.
rows.anchor: { وتذرون الآخرة } قال تدعون { وجوه يومئذ ناضرة }

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummī glosses the faces as radiant.
rows.anchor: { وجوه يومئذ ناضرة } أي مشرقة

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummī says that looking toward God's face means looking toward His mercy and bounty.
rows.anchor: { إلى ربها ناظرة } قال ينظرون إلى وجه الله أي رحمة الله ونعمته

rows.speaker: علي بن موسى الرضا
rows.claim: In a report transmitted through Ibrāhīm ibn Abī Maḥmūd, Imam al-Riḍā explains the faces as radiant and awaiting their Lord's reward.
rows.anchor: قال علي بن موسى الرضا عليه السلام في قوله تعالى { وجوه يومئذ ناضرة

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: The interpretation that the radiant faces await their Lord's reward is also transmitted in al-Tawḥīd, al-Iḥtijāj, and al-Majmaʿ from ʿAlī.
rows.anchor: ورواه في التوحيد والاحتجاج والمجمع عن علي عليه السلام

rows.speaker: المعترضون
rows.claim: Critics object that naẓara meaning “wait” does not take ilā; waiting is transitive without that preposition.
rows.anchor: اعترض على أخذ ناظرة بمعنى منتظرة بأن الانتظار لا يتعدى بإلى بل هو متعد بنفسه

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ answers the grammatical objection with Jamīl ibn Maʿmar's poetic use of naẓara ilā.
rows.anchor: ورد عليه في مجمع البيان بالاستشهاد بقول جميل بن معمر وإذا نظرت إليك من ملك

rows.speaker: شاعر آخر
rows.claim: A second cited poem uses naẓara ilā while describing someone awaiting a promised gift.
rows.anchor: وقول الآخر إني إليك لما وعدت لناظر نظر الفقير إلى الغني الموسر

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf treats “looking” here as a metonymical expression for waiting, an interpretation al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī regards as good.
rows.anchor: وعد في الكشاف إطلاق النظر في الآية بمعنى الانتظار استعمالا كنائيا وهو معنى حسن

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports the Prophet's account that even the lowest in Paradise sees its delights across a thousand years, while its most honored inhabitant sees God's face morning and evening; the Prophet cited these verses.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم إن أدنى أهل الجنة منزلا لمن ينظر إلى جنانه

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that the Prophet explains nāḍirah as whiteness and clarity and says the faces look at Him each day.
rows.anchor: ثم قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم { وجوه يومئذ ناضرة } قال البياض والصفاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report can fit al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī's interpretation; alternatively, God's “face” is His mercy, favor, generosity, and other active attributes, which are what He presents to creation.
rows.anchor: أقول الرواية تقبل الانطباق على المعنى الذي أوردناه في تفسير الآية، ومع الغض عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The face of a thing is what it turns toward another; God's face toward creation is His gracious attributes, so seeing them is seeing His gracious face.
rows.anchor: فإن وجه الشيء ما يستقبل به الشيء غيره وما يستقبل به الله سبحانه خلقه

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet said people see their Lord without modality, a defined limit, or a known attribute.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم في قول الله { وجوه يومئذ ناضرة إلى ربها ناظرة } قال ينظرون إلى ربهم بلا كيفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī takes the report to support inward vision by the heart, not sensory sight by the eye, and to explain Sunni reports that seem to imply anthropomorphic, bounded vision.
rows.anchor: الرواية تؤيد ما قدمنا في تفسير الآية أن المراد به النظر القلبي ورؤية القلب دون العين الحسية

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummī says that when the soul reaches the collarbone someone asks who can treat or recite over him; he knows it is separation, and the final journey is to the Lord of the worlds.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى { كلا إذا بلغت التراقي } قال يعني النفس

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: In al-Kāfī, Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir, answering Jābir, says the dying person asks for a doctor, realizes he is leaving loved ones, and that one leg entwining with the other is the world entwining with the hereafter; the journey is to the Lord of the worlds.
rows.anchor: إلى جابر عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال سألته عن قول الله عز وجل { وقيل من راق وظن أنه الفراق }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This passage presents proofs of God's sole lordship and the Day of Decision, recalls punishment for deniers and blessings for the pious, and reproaches those arrogant toward worship and revelation.
rows.anchor: بيان حجج دالة على توحد الربوبية تقضي بوجود يوم الفصل الذي فيه جزاء المكذبين به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “first” are ancient peoples such as Noah's, ʿĀd's, and Thamūd's; the “later” are subsequent bygone nations joined to them.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالأولين أمثال قوم نوح وعاد وثمود من الأمم القديمة عهدا، وبالآخرين الملحقون بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb natbaʿuhum is nominative as a new sentence, not coordinated with nahlik, which would require the jussive; it means later nations are destroyed after the earlier ones.
rows.anchor: برفع نتبع على الاستيناف وليس بمعطوف على

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause explains the preceding destruction and is set off without a conjunction, as if answering “Why were they destroyed?” with “That is how We deal with criminals.”
rows.anchor: في موضع التعليل لما تقدمه ولذا أورد بالفصل من غير عطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Destroying human criminals is governance of human affairs; since even polytheists acknowledge that God alone destroys them, this proves He is the Lord and there is no other lord or god.
rows.anchor: وهي بعينها حجة على توحد الربوبية فإن إهلاك المجرمين من الانسان تصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Punishment for crimes presupposes a command that people can disobey and recompense for obedience and disobedience; worldly reward and punishment are incomplete, so a Day of Decision must follow.
rows.anchor: ولا معنى للتكليف إلا مع مجازاة المطيع بالثواب والعاصي بالعقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contemptible, low-value, minimally useful water is the semen.
rows.anchor: والماء المهين الحقير قليل الغناء والمراد به النطفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The secure resting place is the womb.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالقرار المكين الرحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The known term is the duration of pregnancy.
rows.anchor: القرار المكين الرحم وبقوله { قدر معلوم } مدة الحمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadarnā derives from qadar, estimation: after creating people, God decrees their coming events and traits, including lifespan, appearance, health, illness, and provision; He is an excellent determiner.
rows.anchor: من القدر بمعنى التقدير، والفاء لتفريع القدر على الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A possible alternative takes qadarnā from qudra, meaning power as opposed to incapacity and God's power over all these matters; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī prefers the estimation reading.
rows.anchor: واحتمل أن يكون { قدرنا } من القدرة مقابل العجز والمراد فقدرنا على جميع ذلك، وما تقدم أوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation and the governance of human development prove sole lordship; lordship entails the creatures' submission and obligation, which requires recompense on a Day of Decision.
rows.anchor: الربوبية تستوجب خضوع المربوبين لساحتها وهو الدين المتضمن للتكليف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains' movement and crushing culminate in their crumbling, scattering, and becoming like loosened sand or fluffed wool, as described in other verses.
rows.anchor: فتسيير الجبال ودكها ينتهي بها إلى بسها ونسفها وصيرورتها كثيبا مهيلا وكالعهن المنفوش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains becoming a mirage cannot mean merely an apparent shimmer like water, since that bears no relation to their being set in motion.
rows.anchor: وأما صيرورتها سرابا بمعنى ما يتوهم ماء لامعا فلا نسبة بين التسيير وبين السراب بهذا المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rather, the mountains' movement erases their existence and reality as mountains: seemingly immovable, substantial peaks become an unreal, empty mirage.
rows.anchor: ينتهي تسييرها إلى انعدامها وبطلان كينونتها وحقيقتها بمعنى كونها جبلا فالجبال الراسيات التي كانت ترى حقائق ذوات كينونة قوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This loss of reality resembles nations destroyed until they became mere tales, and idols that are only names people invented.
rows.anchor: قوله في أقوام أهلكهم وقطع دابرهم، فجعلناهم أحاديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage resembles the image of mountains that look stationary while passing like clouds, if that verse concerns the earthquake of the Hour.
rows.anchor: وترى الجبال تحسبها جامدة وهي تمر مر السحاب

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: Al-Mufradāt defines raṣd as readiness to watch, marṣad as a watch post, and mirṣād as a place specifically appointed for watching.
rows.anchor: قال في المفردات الرصد الاستعداد للترقب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Hell a watch post signals that people must pass over it, as also stated in the verse that none will fail to come to it.
rows.anchor: تنبيها على أن عليها مجاز الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tyrants are those characterized by ṭughyān, going beyond the proper limit.
rows.anchor: الطاغون الملتبسون بالطغيان وهو الخروج عن الحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʾāb is a place of return, from awb, “to return.”
rows.anchor: والمآب اسم مكان من الأوب بمعنى الرجوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is the tyrants' return because they prepared it as their dwelling in worldly life and return to it after leaving this world.
rows.anchor: والعناية في عدها مآبا للطاغين أنهم هيأوها مأوى لأنفسهم وهم في الدنيا ثم إذا انقطعوا عن الدنيا آبوا ورجعوا إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥqāb means many ages and long epochs, with no fixed duration specified here.
rows.anchor: الأحقاب الأزمنة الكثيرة والدهور الطويلة من غير تحديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentators differ on the singular of aḥqāb; one proposed form is ḥuqb, with either a still or doubled ḍamma.
rows.anchor: وهو جمع اختلفوا في واحدة فقيل واحده حقب بالضم فالسكون أو بضمتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of Moses and Pharaoh warns polytheists who deny resurrection and use that denial against religious law, consoles the Prophet over rejection, and threatens his opponents.
rows.anchor: وفيها عظة وإنذار للمشركين المنكرين للبعث وقد توسلوا به إلى رد الدعوة الدينية إذ لا معنى لتشريع الدين لولا المعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destruction of Pharaoh and his army proves Moses' divinely authorized mission; such a mission entails God's lordship over people, contrary to the polytheists' claim that lesser lords govern them.
rows.anchor: ولا تتم رسالته من جانبه تعالى إلا بربوبية منه تعالى للناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening question encourages the listener to hear the story for consolation, warning, and completion of the proof; it is not a request for information.
rows.anchor: استفهام بداعي ترغيب السامع في استماع الحديث ليتسلى به هو ويكون للمنكرين إنذارا بما فيه من ذكر العذاب وإتماما للحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A question that attracts attention to a familiar story is still apt; this may be the first Qur'anic telling or follow a summary in al-Muzzammil and fuller tellings in al-Aʿrāf and Ṭā Hā.
rows.anchor: من الممكن أن تكون الآيات أول ما يقصه الله من قصة موسى أو تكون مسبوقة بذكر قصته كما في سورة المزمل إجمالا

words: إِذْ نَادَىٰهُ رَبُّهُ بِالْوَادِ الْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idh is a temporal adjunct to the story; this was God's first revelation to Moses and His commissioning him as messenger, and Ṭuwā is the name of the sacred valley.
rows.anchor: ظرف للحديث وهو أول ما أوحى الله إليه فقلده الرسالة، وطوى اسم للوادي المقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command explains the divine call; proposals to supply “saying” or an explanatory particle are unnecessary in either construction.
rows.anchor: تفسير للنداء، وقيل الكلام على تقدير القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's transgression is the reason for the command to go to him.
rows.anchor: وقوله { إنه طغى } تعليل للأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An object of ilā is elided: the question means whether Pharaoh is inclined to purify himself.
rows.anchor: متعلق { إلى } محذوف والتقدير هل لك ميل إلى أن تتزكى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purification means cleansing oneself from the filth of tyranny.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالتزكي التطهر من قذارة الطغيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī links fear of God with knowledge and cites the statement that God's learned servants fear Him.
rows.anchor: إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes tazakkā as repentance from tyranny and return to God; the ensuing fear is faith-driven fear that motivates obedience and restrains sin.
rows.anchor: الخشية الملازمة للإيمان الداعية إلى الطاعة والرادعة عن المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If purification means obedience and avoidance of sin, “I will guide you to your Lord, so you will fear” explains that purification by apposition.
rows.anchor: كان قوله { وأهديك إلى ربك فتخشى } مفسرا لما قبله والعطف عطف تفسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fear that follows guidance accords with the statement that God's servants who truly fear Him are the learned.
rows.anchor: إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ is explanatory and the sentence elides “he came to him and called him” before saying that he showed him the sign.
rows.anchor: الفاء فصيحة وفي الكلام حذف وتقدير والأصل فأتاه ودعاه فأراه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great sign is apparently the staff, based on the detailed account; identifying it with all the miracles shown to Pharaoh and his chiefs is remote.
rows.anchor: على ما يظهر من تفصيل القصة آية العصا، وقيل المراد بها مجموع معجزاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh denied Moses and rejected his mission, calling him a sorcerer.
rows.anchor: أي كذب موسى فجحد رسالته وسماه ساحرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disobedience may be to Moses' instruction or to God.
rows.anchor: وعصاه فيما أمره به أو عصى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idbār means turning away, and saʿy means energetic striving; Pharaoh turned away and worked hard to undo Moses' mission and oppose him.
rows.anchor: الإدبار التولي والسعي هو الجد والاجتهاد أي ثم تولى فرعون يجد ويجتهد في إبطال أمر موسى ومعارضته

rows.speaker: طرق أهل السنة
rows.claim: Sunni reports say these verses came when blind Ibn Umm Maktūm entered while the Prophet spoke with Quraysh leaders about Islam; the Prophet frowned, and God reproached him.
rows.anchor: من طرق أهل السنة أن الآيات نزلت في قصة ابن أم مكتوم الأعمى دخل على النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: طرق الشيعة
rows.claim: Some Shiʿi reports also point to Ibn Umm Maktūm's entry and the Prophet's frowning.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض الأخبار من طرق الشيعة إشارة إلى ذلك

rows.speaker: بعض روايات الشيعة
rows.claim: Other Shiʿi reports say the person who frowned was an Umayyad man with the Prophet; he tightened his face when Ibn Umm Maktūm entered.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض روايات الشيعة أن العابس المتولي رجل من بني أمية كان عند النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra rebukes preferring the wealthy and privileged to poor believers, then recalls human dependence on God's care despite ingratitude and turns to resurrection, recompense, and warning.
rows.anchor: فغرض السورة عتاب من يقدم الأغنياء والمترفين على الضعفاء والمساكين من المؤمنين فيرفع أهل الدنيا ويضع أهل الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra is unquestionably Meccan.
rows.anchor: والسورة مكية بلا كلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAbasa means he frowned or tightened his face, and tawallā means he turned away.
rows.anchor: أي بسر وقبض وجهه وأعرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blind man's coming is the reason for the frowning, with the lām of purpose understood.
rows.anchor: تعليل لما ذكر من العبوس بتقدير لام التعليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause beginning “what will make you know” is circumstantial to the subject of “frowned and turned away.”
rows.anchor: حال من فاعل { عبس وتولى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazakkā means becoming pure through good action after reflection; the reflection is taking heed and awakening to true belief.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالتزكي التطهر بعمل صالح بعد التذكر الذي هو الاتعاظ والانتباه للاعتقاد الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder benefits by inviting purification through faith and righteous action; the blind visitor might learn and purify himself or be admonished and remember.
rows.anchor: ونفع الذكرى هو دعوتها إلى التزكي بالإيمان والعمل الصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first two verses speak in the third person, distancing the rebuke; the next two switch to direct address, intensifying reproach and accountability.
rows.anchor: ويزيد شدة بإتيان الآيتين الأوليين في سياق الغيبة لما فيه من الإعراض عن المشافهة والدلالة على تشديد الإنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling him the blind man intensifies the reproach: someone blind, seeking religious guidance out of fear of God, deserved compassion and special attention.
rows.anchor: وفي التعبير عن الجائي بالأعمى مزيد توبيخ لما أن المحتاج الساعي في حاجته إذا كان أعمى فاقدا للبصر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: On the view that the Prophet is the one reproached, third-person wording honors him by implying someone else acted; the later direct address also honors him through intimacy after estrangement.
rows.anchor: وقيل - بناء على كون المراد بالمعاتب هو النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم - أن في التعبير عنه أولا بضمير الغيبة إجلالا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposed honorific reading of the switch from third to second person does not fit the direct address that follows, whose rebuke is stronger and has no conciliatory intimacy.
rows.anchor: وفيه أنه لا يلائمه الخطاب في قوله بعد { أما من استغنى فأنت له تصدى }

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: According to al-Rāghib, ghina, istighnāʾ, taghannī, and taghānī are synonymous.
rows.anchor: الغنى والاستغناء والتغني والتغاني بمعنى على ما ذكره الراغب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The self-sufficient person is the wealthy one whose status and grandeur in others' eyes foster arrogance toward the truth.
rows.anchor: من تلبس بالغنى ولازمه التقدم والرئاسة والعظمة في أعين الناس والاستكبار عن اتباع الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taṣaddā means turning toward something, engaging with it, and attending to its affairs.
rows.anchor: والتصدي التعرض للشيء بالإقبال عليه والإهتمام بأمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuked pattern is that the Prophet attends to wealthy people who scorn the truth, unconcerned whether they purify themselves, while neglecting the person earnestly seeking purification and fearing God.
rows.anchor: أنك تعتني وتقبل على من استغنى واستكبر عن اتباع الحق وما عليك أن لا يزكى وتتلهى وتعرض عمن يجتهد في التزكي وهو يخشى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reading takes mā as negative: it is no fault of yours if the rich man does not purify himself, so eagerness for his conversion should not divert you from one who already accepted Islam.
rows.anchor: قيل { ما } نافية والمعنى وليس عليك بأس أن لا يتزكى حتى يبعثك الحرص

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A second reading takes mā as an incredulous question: what obligation falls on you if he does not cleanse himself of disbelief and sin? You are only a messenger responsible for conveying.
rows.anchor: وقيل { ما } للاستفهام الإنكاري والمعنى وأي شيء يلزمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most contextually apt reading is that the Prophet should not concern himself with the rich man's failure to purify himself; the interrogative reading comes next, and the negative reading is least apt.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى ولا تبالي بعدم تطهره من دنس الكفر والفجور وهذا المعنى أنسب لسياق العتاب ثم الذي قبله ثم الذي قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saʿy literally means walking quickly; in context the man comes hastening to remember and purify himself through religious learning.
rows.anchor: السعي الإسراع في المشي فمعنى قوله { وأما من جاءك يسعى } بحسب ما يفيده المقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He fears God, and fear is a sign of taking the Qur'an's reminder to heart.
rows.anchor: وقوله { وهو يخشى } أي يخشى الله والخشية آية التذكر بالقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Talahhā means occupying or distracting yourself from him with someone else.
rows.anchor: أي تتلهى وتتشاغل بغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting anta and the pronouns lahu and ʿanhu emphasizes and fixes the reproach.
rows.anchor: وتقديم ضمير { أنت } في قوله { فأنت له تصدى } وقوله { فأنت عنه تلهى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā is a deterrent against frowning, turning away, attending to the self-sufficient, and neglecting those who fear God.
rows.anchor: } { كلا } ردع عما عوتب عليه من العبوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun may refer to the Qur'anic verses or the Qur'an; it is feminine because the predicate tadhkira is feminine.
rows.anchor: والضمير في { إنها تذكرة } للآيات القرآنية أو للقرآن وتأنيث الضمير لتأنيث الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is an admonition for those who take admonition and a reminder of true belief and action.
rows.anchor: والمعنى إن الآيات القرآنية أو القرآن تذكرة أي موعظة يتعظ بها من اتعاظ أو مذكر يذكر حق الاعتقاد والعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is parenthetical; its pronoun refers either to the Qur'an or to the truths it reminds people of.
rows.anchor: وقوله { فمن شاء ذكره } جملة معترضة والضمير للقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase gestures to guidance from the innate disposition that preserves true belief and action, and implies no coercion: the caller gains nothing; the person who remembers benefits.
rows.anchor: وفي التعبير بهذا التعبير { فمن شاء ذكره } تلويح إلى أن لا إكراه في الدعوة إلى التذكر فلا نفع فيها

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ says ṣuḥuf is the plural of ṣaḥīfa; Arabs call anything written on a sheet a ṣaḥīfa or book, whether on parchment or another material.
rows.anchor: قال في المجمع الصحف جمع صحيفة، والعرب تسمي كل مكتوب فيه صحيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fī ṣuḥuf is a predicate following another predicate of inna; the apparent sense is that the Qur'an is written on multiple sheets in the hands of revelation angels.
rows.anchor: و { في صحف } خبر بعد خبر لأن وظاهره أنه مكتوب في صحف متعددة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sheets are not the Preserved Tablet: the plural wording does not fit, since God never calls that tablet “sheets,” “books,” or “tablets” in the plural.
rows.anchor: وهذا يضعف القول بأن المراد بالصحف اللوح المحفوظ ولم يرد في كلامه تعالى إطلاق الصحف ولا الكتب ولا الألواح بصيغة الجمع على اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sheets are not the books of earlier prophets, since that reading does not fit the apparent description “in the hands of emissaries.”
rows.anchor: كتب الأنبياء الماضين لعدم ملاءمته لظهور قوله { بأيدي سفرة } الخ في أنه صفة لصحف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mukarramah means honored, marfūʿah elevated in rank with God, and muṭahharah purified from falsehood, idle speech, doubt, and contradiction.
rows.anchor: مكرمة } أي معظمة، وقوله { مرفوعة } أي قدرا عند الله، وقوله { مطهرة } أي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bi-aydī safarah is another adjective of the sheets; safarah means envoys or messengers (singular safīr), while noble describes their persons and virtuous describes their deeds.
rows.anchor: بأيدي سفرة كرام بررة } صفة بعد صفة لصحف، والسفرة هم السفراء جمع سفير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is a reminder written in multiple honored, elevated, pure sheets, carried by angels noble to God in essence and virtuous in their actions.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الآيات أن القرآن تذكرة مكتوبة في صحف متعددة معظمة مرفوعة قدرا مطهرا من كل دنس وقذارة بأيدي سفراء من الملائكة كرام على ربهم بطهارة ذواتهم بررة عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses indicate that angels carry the sheets and convey their Qur'an under Gabriel's command; attributing revelation to them does not conflict with attributing it to Gabriel.
rows.anchor: ويظهر من الآيات أن للوحي ملائكة يتصدون لحمل الصحف وإيحاء ما فيها من القرآن فهم أعوان جبريل وتحت أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel is obeyed by the angels acting under him, so their delivery can be attributed to him; likewise the taking of souls by the Angel of Death's assistants is attributed to him, and both are ultimately God's acts.
rows.anchor: والإيحاء الذي هو فعل أعوانه فعله كما أن فعله وفعلهم جميعا فعل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view identifies the safarah as angelic scribes; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī considers his messenger interpretation clearer.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالسفرة الكتاب من الملائكة والذي تقدم من المعنى أجلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies the safarah as people who write and read the Qur'an; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī dismisses this reading.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بهم القراء يكتبونها ويقرؤونها وهو كما ترى

rows.speaker: مجمع البيان
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ recounts that Abdullah ibn Shurayḥ ibn Mālik ibn Rabīʿa al-Fihri, Ibn Umm Maktūm, interrupted the Prophet's appeal to ʿUtba, Abū Jahl, al-ʿAbbās, Ubayy, and Umayya ibn Khalaf to ask for teaching; the Prophet frowned, fearing the elites would scorn followers who were blind or enslaved, then turned back to them.
rows.anchor: في المجمع قيل نزلت الآيات في عبد الله بن أم مكتوم وهو عبد الله بن شريح بن مالك بن ربيعة الفهروي
